subject: GlobeRetail TTFT & streaming requirements — recap and action plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@payments.ai>, ops+infra@globeretail.com
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: GlobeRetail TTFT & streaming requirements — recap and action plan

Hi Samir / GlobeRetail infra team —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and a proposed action plan so we have alignment on the latency / streaming SLOs and what the pilot should measure. Please flag anything missing.

What we heard from your side:
- Target TTFT (time-to-first-token): <= 300 ms (95th) for interactive product flows (cart/checkout assistant).
- Preferred streaming transport: SSE for simplicity; WebSocket acceptable as fallback for long-lived sessions.
- Chunk cadence: ~150–300 ms between chunks for natural UX (you prefer shorter first chunk).
- Concurrency & throughput: peak concurrency ~600 simultaneous users; expected sustained ~180 req/s during flash sales, spiking to ~350 req/s for short bursts.
- Typical output size: 150–300 tokens per response (median ~180).
- Integration constraints: VPC peering preferred; must provide request-level telemetry for SLA reporting.

Redwood initial assessment / asks:
- To reach ~300 ms TTFT we recommend a low-batching profile (disable large collective batching), aggressive KV cache warmup, and an SSE-optimized tail path. We should benchmark both hosted and dedicated pool variants.
- We need your representative request traces (anonymized examples) and a replayable prompt set to size the pilot.
- For the pilot, propose we validate at 200 req/s sustained, 350 req/s burst, and a simulated 600 concurrent connections (SSE) for 30m windows.

Next steps / owners:
1) GlobeRetail: share an anonymized sample of 50–100 typical requests + expected token length by EOD Wed Jan 14 — Samir / ops team.
2) Redwood (Diego): run microbenchmarks against model variants and streaming configs, deliver initial TTFT/throughput matrix by Mon Jan 19.
3) Redwood (Marissa): prepare a pilot quote and proposed MAP (mutual action plan) with milestone dates — draft by Fri Jan 16.
4) Schedule technical pilot kickoff: Tue Jan 20 (30–45m) — I'll send calendar invite once we confirm availability.

Attachments: GlobeRetail_TTFT_requirements_v1.pdf (see section 2 for sample UX cadence).

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: GlobeRetail_TTFT_requirements_v1.pdf (pdf, 48KB)]

From: Samir Shah <samir@payments.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+infra@globeretail.com, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GlobeRetail TTFT & streaming requirements — recap and action plan

Thanks Hannah — this looks good and captures the priorities. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- The 300 ms 95th TTFT target is aspirational for the main checkout flow; for search/autocomplete we can accept up to 450 ms. Can we test both profiles?
- For SSE vs WS: SSE is fine for browser-based sessions. We do have a small set of mobile clients that prefer WebSocket. Would like confirmation that Redwood supports both inside the same pilot and can route fallback automatically.
- Concurrency: the 600 concurrent is a conservative upper bound — it's concurrent clients, not simultaneous requests. Some of our users open multiple streaming channels. Please simulate that pattern.

I attached a short CSV with token length histogram and a tiny example of a request (anonymized).

Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Platform, GlobeRetail
[sample_requests.csv attached]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir@payments.ai>, ops+infra@globeretail.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 10:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GlobeRetail TTFT & streaming requirements — recap and action plan

Hannah / Marissa —

Quick technical note after reviewing Samir's CSV and our internal perf rigs:

1) TTFT levers we will exercise:
   - Disable collective batching for the checkout flow (single-request low-latency path).
   - Keep KV cache warm for common prefixes (reduces autoregeneration work for multi-turn prompts).
   - Prefer an int8 quantized variant for the pilot if quality checks pass — reduces per-token compute.

2) Streaming cadence handling:
   - We can prioritize a larger first chunk (~50–80 tokens) to shorten perceived TTFT, then 150–300 ms cadence for subsequent chunks. That handles your UX ask of a short first chunk.
   - SSE and WebSocket are both supported; we can route based on client type. We'll instrument fallback logic in the pilot.

3) Pilot config proposal (microbenchmark targets):
   - Model variant: open-llm-v2 / int8 (fallback to fp16 if quality regression).
   - Endpoint config: 4 backends (GPU) with concurrency slots tuned for low queuing; simulate 200 req/s sustained, 350 req/s 10-min burst, and a 600-client connect test for 30m.
   - Metrics to capture: p50/p90/p95 TTFT, end-to-end latency, chunk cadence distribution (ms), token-rate, error/retry rates, and resource utilization (GPU % / mem / NVLink).

Action: I'll spin up the first microbench by Friday Jan 16 using the sample CSV and send raw results plus a short runbook on what to measure. If we miss the 300 ms 95th, we'll iterate on instance sizing and reduction of cold paths.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment stub: bench-config.yaml]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@payments.ai>, ops+infra@globeretail.com
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: GlobeRetail TTFT pilot — confirmed plan & next steps

Hi Samir —

Quick update and confirmed action plan after Diego's bench note. Thanks for the sample data — it was helpful. Summary of agreed items and deadlines: 

1) Data we still need (GlobeRetail) — please upload to the Drive link by Wed Jan 21:
   - Anonymized request traces (50–100) + token-length histogram (you already sent a partial CSV).
   - Network egress/IP ranges for VPC peering test (if proceeding with private pilot).

2) Redwood deliverables:
   - Microbenchmark report (Diego) — initial TTFT/throughput matrix by Mon Jan 19 (attached).
   - Pilot MAP & quote (Marissa) — draft delivered Fri Jan 16; updated to include dedicated pool pricing for low-latency path.

3) Pilot kickoff call: Tue Jan 20, 10:30–11:15 PT — invite sent. Agenda: bench review, pilot topology, telemetry hooks, and success criteria.

Acceptance criteria (mutual):
- 95th percentile TTFT <= 300 ms for checkout profile; search profile p95 <= 450 ms.
- SSE-first experience for browsers with WS fallback for mobile.
- Ability to report p50/p90/p95 TTFT and chunk cadence per route in Console.

Attachments: GR-MAP-2026Q1.xlsx (mutual action plan, milestones), bench-results-initial.pdf (Diego).

If this looks good I'll mark the deal stage to 'Pilot — technical' in HubSpot and proceed with the calendar invite.

Thanks again —
Hannah
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: GR-MAP-2026Q1.xlsx (xlsx, 12KB), bench-results-initial.pdf (pdf, 220KB)]
